**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 63, verses 1–7:**

Madaniyya (Medinan), with seven hundred and seventy-six letters, one hundred and eighty words, and eleven verses.

Al-Hadi informed us, saying: Tabgharan related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dawud related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Asim related to us, saying: Shababa related to us, saying: Makhlad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid related to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from Dharr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Munafiqun will be cleared of hypocrisy." In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say: "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars.﴾ That is, in what they display, because they conceal the opposite of it.

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, a cover, ﴿and they bar others from the way of Allah. Evil is what they have been doing.﴾ ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts, and so they do not understand.﴾ ﴿When you see them, their bodies impress you﴾, due to the evenness of their form, the beauty of their appearance, and the height of their stature.

Ibn 'Abbas said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy was a large, healthy, eloquent man with a sharp tongue. When he spoke, the Prophet (peace be upon him) would listen to his words.

﴿And if they speak, you listen to what they say﴾, ﴿as though they were propped-up timber﴾, figures without spirits, and bodies without minds.

Al-A'mash, al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Amr, from 'Asim, and it is said from 'Abbas, read ﴿khushb﴾ with a light pronunciation, with the shin vowelless. This is the reading of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib and the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, who said: "Its basis in the Arabic language is that its singular is khashaba, and you do not find in their speech a noun of the pattern fu'la (plural) of the form fa'l, with the fa' and 'ayn vowelled with a damma. It would also necessitate that the word for camels (al-budn) be read in the same way, as in ﴿wal-budna ja'alnaha lakum﴾ [the sacrificial camels, We have made them for you], because its singular is also badana."

The others read it with the heavy pronunciation (shadda on the shin, khushshub), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. There is a difference of report about it from Ibn Kathir and 'Asim.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Muhammad al-Hamshadhi informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Musa related to us, saying: al-Asma'i related to us, saying: Sulaym al-'Amili related to us, saying: A man came to Ibn Sirin and said: "I saw in my sleep that I was embracing a piece of wood." He said: "I think you are one of the people of this verse," and he recited ﴿as though they were propped-up timber﴾.

﴿They think every cry is against them﴾, out of their cowardice, their bad opinion, and their lack of certainty.

Muqatil said: It means that if a caller calls out in the camp, or a beast of burden bolts, or a lost animal is searched for, they think they are being targeted, because of the terror in their hearts.

Some of them said: He only said this because they are apprehensive that Allah will send down something about them, exposing their secrets and making their blood and wealth lawful. And a poet said on this theme:

*"Even if it were a sparrow, you would think it / a marked one calling out to slaves and bastards."* [[al-Sihah: 5/1946.]]

Then He said: ﴿They are the enemy﴾, as a beginning and a predicate.

﴿So beware of them and do not trust them.﴾

﴿May Allah destroy them﴾, meaning: may Allah curse them.

﴿How are they deluded?﴾ That is, how are they turned away from the truth.

﴿And when it is said to them: "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads﴾, meaning they incline them and show with their faces a display of aversion.

Nafi', al-Mufaddal, and Ya'qub, through the narration of Rawh, and Zayd read it with the light pronunciation of the waw (lawwaw), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim.

The rest read it with the heavy pronunciation, and Abu 'Ubayda chose it, saying: "Because they did it again and again."

﴿And you see them turning away﴾, that is, turning away from what they were called to, ﴿while they are arrogant﴾, not asking forgiveness.

﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ This verse was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, the hypocrite, and his companions. This is what the people of exegesis and the historians have mentioned: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received word that the Banu al-Mustaliq were gathering to fight him, and their leader was al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar, Abu Juwayriya, the husband of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) heard of them, he set out toward them until he met them at a water source of theirs called al-Muraysi', on the side toward the coast. The people clashed and fought, and Allah defeated the Banu al-Mustaliq; He killed whoever among them was killed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took their children, women, and wealth, and Allah granted them to him as spoils (fay').

A man from the Muslims, from the Banu Kulayb ibn 'Awf ibn 'Amir, called Hisham ibn Sababa, was struck; a man from the Ansar, of the clan of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, struck him, thinking he was from the enemy, and killed him by mistake.

While the people were at that water, a group of people came to it, and with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was a hired man of his from the Banu 'Ammar called Jahjaha ibn Sa'id, who was leading his horse. Jahjaha and Sinan al-Juhani, an ally of the Banu 'Awf of al-Khazraj, pushed each other at the water, and they fought. The Juhani cried out: "O company of the Ansar!" and the Ghifari cried out: "O company of the Muhajirun!" Jahjaha the Ghifari was helped by a man of the Muhajirun called Ja'al, who was poor. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said to Ja'al: "Are you really there?" He replied: "What prevents me from doing that?" Ja'al's tongue became harsh against 'Abd Allah. 'Abd Allah said: "By Him by whom one swears, I will make you and your like leave this place." 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy became angry, and with him were a group of his people, including Zayd ibn Arqam, a youth of young age. Ibn Ubayy said: "Do it! They have contended with us and outnumbered us in our land. By Allah, our likeness and theirs is only as the speaker said: 'Fatten your dog and it will eat you.' Indeed, by Allah, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble from it." By "the more honorable" he meant himself, and by "the more humble" he meant the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Then he turned to those of his people who were present and said: "This is what you have done to yourselves: you let them settle in your lands and you shared your wealth with them. By Allah, if you withheld food from Ja'al and his dependents, they would not ride upon your necks, and they would soon move away from your lands and join their tribes and clients. So do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse from around Muhammad."

Zayd ibn Arqam said: "By Allah, you are the humiliated, the hated among your people, while Muhammad is in the might of the Most Gracious and the affection of the Muslims. By Allah, I will not love you after these words of yours."

'Abd Allah said: "Be quiet, I was only joking." Zayd ibn Arqam went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), after he had finished the expedition, and informed him of the news, while 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him. 'Umar said: "Let me strike his neck, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "If he threatens, leave him alone; he will enter [the fold]." 'Umar said: "As for when the command of the Prophet (peace be upon him) comes, 'Umar sets out..." and he did not stay more than a few days, and he [Ibn Ubayy] ... "you thought I was ill," and he died.

They said: When this verse was revealed, and the lie of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy became clear, it was said to him: "O Abu Hubab, it has been revealed about you, so go to the Messenger of Allah so that he may ask forgiveness for you." He turned his head and said: "You ordered me to believe, and I have believed; you ordered me to give the zakat of my wealth, and I have given it. Nothing remains except that I prostrate to Muhammad." Then Allah, glory be to Him, revealed ﴿And when it is said to them: "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you"﴾, up to His words ﴿They are the ones who say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse." And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth﴾. So no one can give anything here except by His permission, nor withhold anything except by His will.

A man said to Hatim al-Asamm: "From where does he eat?" He recited ﴿And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.﴾

Al-Junayd said: "The treasures of the heavens are the unseen matters, and the treasures of the earth are the hearts; and He is the Knower of the unseen and the Turner of hearts." And al-Shibli used to say: ﴿And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth﴾, so where are you going?

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 63, verses 8–11:

They say, "If we return to Medina—" meaning, from the expedition against Banu Lihyan and then Banu al-Mustaliq, who were a tribe of Hudhayl— "the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it."

﴿But might belongs to God, to His Messenger, and to the believers.﴾ So the might of God, glorified is He, is His subduing whatever is other than Him; the might of His Messenger is the manifestation of his religion over all other religions; and the might of the believers is His granting them victory over their enemies, so they are the ones who prevail.

It is also said: the might of God is (His) guardianship (wilaya). God, exalted is He, says: ﴿There, guardianship belongs to God, the Truth﴾ [18:44]. The might of the Messenger is (His) sufficiency. God, glorified is He, says: ﴿We are sufficient for you against the mockers﴾ [15:95]. The might of the believers is elevation and care. God, glorified is He, says: ﴿And you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾ [3:139], and He says: ﴿And He is ever Kind and Merciful to the believers﴾ [33:43].

It is also said: the might of God is lordship (rububiyya), the might of the Messenger is prophethood (nubuwwa), and the might of the believers is servitude ('ubudiyya).

Ja'far al-Sadiq used to say: "Who is like me, when the Lord of the Throne is my Worshipped One? Who is like me, when You are mine?"

It is also said: the might of God is five-fold: the might of dominion and permanence, the might of greatness and pride, the might of giving and bestowing, the might of elevation and self-sufficiency, and the might of majesty and splendour. The might of the Messenger is five-fold: the might of precedence and beginning, the might of the call to prayer and proclamation, the might of the "sure standing of truth" before the prophets, the might of choice and selection, and the might of prevailing over enemies. The might of the believers is five-fold: the might of delay, its evidence being: "We are the first and the last" ; the might of ease, its evidence being: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [54:17] and ﴿God intends for you ease﴾ [2:185]; the might of glad tidings, its evidence being: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from God a great bounty﴾ [33:47]; the might of honour, its evidence being: ﴿And you will have the upper hand﴾ [3:139]; and the might of increase, and its evidence being: they are the most numerous of nations.

﴿But most of the hypocrites do not know.﴾ [Note in the manuscript: "(But most of mankind do not know)" which is an error.]

﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you﴾ — meaning, let them not occupy you — ﴿from the remembrance of God.﴾ The exegetes said: this means the five daily prayers. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God﴾ [24:37], the verse in full.

﴿And whoever does that, those are the losers.﴾ ﴿And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, why did You not delay me﴾ — give me respite — ﴿for a brief term﴾ — meaning, as much as You delayed in this world — ﴿so I could give charity and be among the righteous.﴾ It is permissible that (lā) be superfluous, so the statement carries the sense of wishing; and it is permissible that it mean "why not" (halla), in which case it is interrogative.

﴿for a brief term﴾: meaning, as much as You delayed in this world; ﴿so I could give charity﴾: so I might give alms and purify my wealth.

﴿and be among the righteous﴾: the believers. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿and whoever of their fathers were righteous﴾ [13:23]. This is the view of Muqatil and a group of exegetes, and they said: this verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites.

It is also said: the righteous here means the Hajj, and the verse was revealed concerning the believers.

al-Dahhak and Atiyya narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: No one dies who had wealth and did not pay its zakat, and was able to perform Hajj but did not perform it, without asking to return at the time of death. They said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, fear God! We see that this disbeliever asked to return." He said: "I will recite to you a Qur'an," and then he recited this verse up to His saying: ﴿so I could give charity and be among the righteous.﴾ He said: "I will perform Hajj." We were informed by Ibn Manjawayh, who said: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, who said: Ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, who said: Salama narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, who said: al-Thawri informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Hayya, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas.

The readers differed concerning His saying ﴿wa-akun﴾ (and I would be). Abu 'Amr and Ibn Muhays read ﴿wa-akūna﴾ with a waw and a fatha on the nun, as an answer to the wish, or, with the fa', as an interrogative. Abu 'Amr said: the waw was dropped from the codex by way of abbreviation, just as they dropped it in (kullaman), whose original form has a waw.

al-Farra' said: I saw in some codices of 'Abd Allah [ibn Mas'ud] ﴿fa-aqūlā﴾ / ﴿fa-qulā﴾ without a waw. Confirming this reading is what Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us, who said: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, who said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, who said: al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said: in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, it reads "wa-akūna min al-ṣāliḥīn" with a waw.

The others read with the jazm: ﴿wa-akun﴾, coordinating it with ﴿fa-asaddaq﴾. Had the fa' not been there, ﴿fa-asaddaq﴾ would have been jussive. Abu 'Ubayd chose the jazm, and said: for three reasons:

First: I found it in the codex of the Imam 'Uthman, ﴿wa-akun﴾ without the waw, and the codices then agreed on this, so they did not differ.

Second: the agreement of most readers of the regions upon it.

Third: we found for it a sound grammatical basis that no one learned in the discipline would be ignorant of, namely that it is a coordination with the position of ﴿asaddaq﴾ before the fa' was introduced. We have found a similar example in their ancient poetry, among which is the saying of a poet:

"So test me with your trial, perhaps I ... may reconcile with you and win over Nawiyy" [Lisan al-'Arab 11/474].

Here "wa-yastadrij" is jussive, coordinated with the position of "uṣālihukum" before "la'alla" entered.

﴿And God will never delay a soul when its term has come; and God is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ Read with the yā' (ya'malūn); others read it with the tā' (ta'malūn).

Here "wa-yastadrij" is jussive, coordinated with the position of "uṣālihukum" before "la'alla" entered.
